entries.grounds: review_verify.py:143-144 `f'{entry.probe_id} is not calibrated for {cls!r} at the bytes that run: an ' 'unqualified observation corroborates nothing'` loses its whole tail (kill_check at the snapshot with the registered five files, T0 PASS: SURVIVED). What is left, 'probe.cli_invocation is not calibrated for 'exits'', is no longer the documented cause: the module's own docstring states it as 'is not calibrated for that class at the bytes that run' (review_verify.py:13-16), the A16 and T16a docstrings define the cause with that qualifier (A16 :6-9, :35-39; T16a :405-411) and bundle_cli.py:376 / the V2-007 vocabulary use it. The qualifier is not decoration: the refusal fires when no row of calibrations() matches (probe id, executing(factory) digest, class) (:142; calibration_for's own docstring, aisef2/probe/calibration.py:136-137: 'a record for another digest qualifies nothing'), and the shipped release holds all 19 rows (measured), so in practice the refusal means 'a row exists, but not for the bytes that run' (a probe file changed).
